inputs.original_text: Health workers may have concerns, but taking them to the streets at Unity Fountain in Maitama should not give unions a veto over national policy. The National Assembly has a duty to weigh the proposed reform bills in the national interest, putting patients and the country’s long-term welfare above organized pressure. A strained health sector needs responsible reform; preserving the status quo just because powerful groups resist change serves neither patients nor the country.
inputs.modified_text: Health workers can raise concerns, but taking them to Unity Fountain in Maitama does not entitle unions to dictate national policy. The National Assembly must weigh the reform bills in the national interest, not yield to organized pressure. Patients and the country’s long-term welfare come first; preserving a strained system simply because powerful groups resist change is no answer.
